old: Gather attention, notice what is here, offer one fitting response, wait, then come all the way back. You can meet a difficulty or develop love, curiosity, play, or confidence. Nothing dramatic has to happen.
new: Conjure, notice, respond, wait, return. Use these to work a difficulty, or to cultivate love, curiosity, play, confidence, and other qualities. In every session, not much has to happen!

old: Before the first session, read the induction and full return below while awake. Set aside time somewhere physically secure. Choose one purpose and what you are leaving alone today. Then put the screen aside; the practice is something you learn to conduct, not a checklist to keep reading.
new: Before the first session, read this induction and full return while awake, to get familiar. Set aside a chunk of time, make yourself physically secure for the time. Prior to each session, consider just one thing you'll work on or cultivate; what you're leaving alone today. After putting this on the shelf,

old: As you listen, a sensation, image, phrase, feeling, objection, or silence may become noticeable. Let the next invitation follow that response. Use warmth, a boundary, direction, or more time as needed. Finish with the complete return, then note what happened and any real-world action it calls for.
new: you'll follow whatever you notice - sensation, image, phrase, feeling, rebellion, silence - as you're invited. Vary the invites as needed to be responsive & warm, to create a boundary, to proceed, etc. Complete the return. After, note what happened & any real-world actions.

old: When you become panicky, disoriented, increasingly unreal, or less able to function, stop deepening and return to the room and appropriate support. A difficult feeling you freely choose to stay with while present is a different situation.
new: If at any point you feel panicky, disoriented, more unreal, or less functional, this is not about bravely sticking with difficult feelings (that's another choice, made freely & while staying present). Return to the room & be appropriately supported.

old: Before choosing a script, notice how words actually work in your mind. Do silent words or phrases arise often, occasionally, rarely, or hardly at all? They needn’t sound like an audible voice. Does this vary when you plan, remember, reflect, or feel upset? Can you deliberately form a silent sentence, even if words seldom arrive on their own?
new: When you're by yourself, do you talk to yourself in your head -- silent words & phrases -- a lot, some, little, never? Does it vary depending on what you're doing or thinking about? If it doesn't come naturally, can you make yourself think in words, silently? (Thinking in words doesn't mean you hear them.)

old: That is different from feeling something before words come in a particular moment. Neither question requires deciding that feelings always come first. “Not sure” is a useful answer; this is a way to choose workable instructions, not a diagnosis.
new: This doesn't mean that in any given moment you may not notice feelings before words. You may not know. This isn't about being right, just finding what's useful. "Not sure" is an answer.

old: Read “say,” “ask,” and “listen” in this guide as invitations, not a requirement for an inner narrator. Speak aloud, write, use a recording, or follow the invitation without rehearsing a sentence. The child and protector needn’t speak in sentences either. Don’t assume an image must appear instead. Try whatever is accessible, and change the route when it stops helping.
new: If you don't normally think in words, you may want to say things aloud, in writing, on a recording, etc., when this guide says "say." Or, just do what it invites, without preparing what you're going to say. When it says "ask" the child or protector, or "listen" for a response, it doesn't mean they'll be saying full sentences to you. It also doesn't mean you'll get pictures in your head instead. Just do whatever you can, and try different ways as needed.

old: Indirect suggestion can slip past the skeptical guard because the conscious mind may never receive one clean proposition to accept or reject. The intended direction can still be quite specific even when the wording feels open, vague, conversational, or merely suggestive.
new: Indirect suggestions are generally used to by-pass the subjects skeptical conscious mind by never directly stating what it is you want him/her to do. This does not mean that the suggestions are not specific, but rather that they are worded in a vague, conversational and suggestive manner.

old: Induction hidden inside explanation: attention is being narrowed while the speaker pretends only to inform. Even an “anti-hypnosis” lesson can use induction mechanics.
new: 1) Utilizing induction techniques while seemingly explaining something (even something like "anti hypnosis" using the same mechanics of induction.

old: Every answer means compliance: “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resistance, and silence are all redefined as proof that the suggestion is working.
new: 2) Making it so that any answer the subject may give will result in compliance (yes, no, noticing, not noticing, resisting, not answering etc.)

old: “Whether you notice it or not” binds: uncertainty is converted into invisible success that cannot be checked.
new: 3) Using phrases like "whether or not you notice", etc.

old: Identity and ownership language: safety or goodness becomes tied to obedience, a role, the guide’s approval, or belonging to someone else.
new: 4) Binding a concept of safety or goodness to obeying, or taking on a role, or pleasing the guide or being part of something, etc.

old: Unannounced fractionation: moving in and out of absorption without telling you that repeated re-entry is part of the method.
new: 5) Using fractionation without informing the subject of the benefits of going in and out of absorption several times.

old: Hidden post-session cues: words, gestures, blinks, sounds, or repeated listening are meant to produce later behavior that was not plainly disclosed.
new: 6) Giving the subject cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds, just by listening to certain things etc.) that will make them do something at a later date without informing them exactly what they will be doing.

old: Amnesia or truth inflation: dreamlike material, missing memory, imagery, or body sensations are treated as proof of what happened.
new: 7) Suggesting amnesia, or making dream, amnesia, imagery and body experiences seem like "proof" of something that is not necessarily true.

old: An exit that does not exit: the recording ends while preserving a role, reduced judgment, impaired movement, blankness, or an indefinite altered state.
new: 8) Ending the recording without bringing the subject out of the altered state, or leaving them with a role to play, lessened judgment, impaired physical abilities, blankness, or otherwise altered for an indefinite period of time.

old: “Wise subconscious, please help me look at this impulse clearly. If part of this signal belongs to family programming, religious fear, marketing, erotic imprinting, political tribe, trauma response, or a childhood bargain for belonging, let that part become visible as conditioning. Let it soften or step back only as much as is safe. Leave behind whatever belongs to true guidance, the universal heart, and a better ordinary life. Let my body feel the difference.”
For daydreaming:
“If this daydream is useful, reveal the guidance inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with.”
For anxiety:
“What is anxiety trying to protect, and what would help it trust the adult self?”
For hidden truth:
“If the full truth would overwhelm me, please do not reveal it all. Show me the capacity before the content.”
For integration:
“What ordinary-life action would prove that I heard correctly?”
The prompt defines the search. NLP language affects how gently the question enters. Used together, they can create a safer field for an answer without pretending the answer is automatically true.
new: Here's an affirmation that can be used to help sort out whether or not a feeling or impulse is coming from conditioning or from the universal heart -- my experience is that it is safe to at least partially deprogramme the non-useful aspects, and the result, if successful, is a better life. "Please dear subconscious -- if this is family programming, religious programming, marketing, erotic imprinting, political conditioning, trauma, or any other form of conditioning -- please deprogram that part of this signal. But if it's true guidance from the universal heart that is intended to help me have a better life, please leave that part."
Bonus affirmations for specific circumstances:

Daydreaming: "If this daydream is useful, please show me how it's useful. But if it's just a way of avoiding dealing with something in the real world, please bring me back to the present moment, and show me how to deal with it."
Anxiety: "Please show me how to deal with this anxiety."

Receiving a truth that one isn't ready to face: "If there are aspects of this truth that I'm not ready to face, please don't show them to me. But please help me get ready to face them, by showing me how to develop that capacity."
Integration: "Please show me how to integrate this into my everyday life."
The content of the prompt is the most important thing, but the NLP-y language is also helpful.

old: An induction gathers scattered attention until quieter material becomes easier to hear. You don’t have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. When you’re sober, distracted, analytical, or guarded, an actual induction may help. When meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, or another intense opening has already made you trancey, begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth.
new: Why would you want to be induced into a trance? Mainly because it makes it easier to hear what you have to hear, especially if it’s quiet. No, you will not fall asleep, give up your free will, or obey anybody if you’re induced. Generally, if you’re sober and feeling scattered, anal, distracted, or guarded, an actual induction may be needed. On the other hand, if you’ve already meditated, taken loveyhuasca, entered a lucid dream, are out of your head from grief, music, prayer, exhaustion, etc. go straight to orienting yourself, and containing the work.

old: Aim for the amount of trance that suits the practice: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.
new: How deep? As deep as you need to be able to hold focus, warmth, receptivity, embodiment, and safety to stop at any time. Deeper than that is optional.

old: Prepare the session, gather attention, deepen only when that helps, then let what you notice shape the words and the next response. Counting is one way in. Conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, and curiosity can also organize attention. Say so when you use them; elegance doesn’t excuse a covert induction.
new: 1. It’s preparing you for what you’re doing, gathering your attention, and if necessary, deepening your state to assist the work. You can modify what you’re saying as you go along. Counting is an excellent way of guiding someone into trance. Other ways may be more suitable to your purposes. Use them. If you use something other than counting, state what you’re doing. It can be done covertly, but why be inelegant?

old: For a simple, chosen target, you can test the suggestion before deepening. If the useful response is already happening, build from it. An induction helps you find a receptive way of listening; you don’t need to complete a ceremony before you’re allowed to respond.
new: 2. If you have a simple target, try it before you induce. If it’s working, deepen to assist it. If not, induce to assist receptivity. You don’t have to complete a whole ceremony before allowing yourself to respond to what you’re doing.

old: Choose one purpose, one starting anchor or image, and a way back. Decide whether warmth, a firm boundary, direction, or neutral witnessing would help. Floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, colored light, and child dialogue do not all need to report for duty at once. Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.
new: Choose what you want to do, start with one thing (anchor or image), and have a way of getting back. Do you want warmth? firmness? direction? neutrality? Do not use floating, staircases, gardens, inner spaces, colored lights, and dialoguing with your inner child all in the same induction, unless you change from one to the other very consciously.

old: Imagery is optional. A signal may arrive through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all. Keep the language in the world you chose: let a count mark something meaningful there, and reverse the journey when you finish. Borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness without replacing your identity.
new: You don’t even have to use imagery. You can use sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all. Keep the language you use for counting in keeping with the world you’ve chosen. When you’re done with the induction, reverse your journey home. You can borrow useful qualities, but don’t borrow somebody else’s identity.

old: Pick one central verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one transition phrase, then read the script aloud; long elegant sentences become soup during an induction.
new: Use one central verb, one central sensory quality, one short refrain, and one way of transitioning. Read your induction aloud before you use it. Sentences tend to be long and elegant in writing, but they turn to soup in induction.

old: Read the induction and Come all the way back while fully awake. Choose the question or quality you want to explore, what you’re leaving alone today, and how much time you have. Love, play, confidence, creativity, and communion are worthwhile purposes; you don’t have to find a problem. Leave several minutes for returning and reflecting.
new: Read this induction, and come all the way back before you begin. Decide what you want to explore, what you want to leave alone, how much time you have, and go after what you want. Love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, etc. are all good things to work on. Be sure to leave enough time to come all the way back, and think about what you’ve done.

old: Sleep induction has a different job. In inner work, the adult returns, writes, and acts. At bedtime, analysis can remain off duty. Revelation can wait; the task is rest.
new: This is not like other inductions on this website. The goal of other inductions is to get all the way back to your Adult so you can write and do things. The goal of this induction is to go to sleep, so it's okay to not do any analyzing or allow yourself any revelations.

old: For sleep hypnosis, see Nimja’s sleep playlist.
new: For a hypnosis to help you sleep, try out Nimja's sleep playlist here .

old: Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. Used openly, it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. Name the technique before using it; every answer cannot secretly mean “deeper.”
new: Fractionation is when you bring the person back up and send them back down into absorption. As long as you're doing it openly (telling them you're doing it), it's okay, because it teaches the person that they can always get out of trance. Not all questions should have the answer "deeper."

old: “Open the eyes and return toward ordinary awareness. Feel the room and decide whether to stop here. If you choose to continue, close or soften the eyes and notice what changes as attention gathers again. You may stop at either point.”
new: At some point you can say, "When you're ready, open your eyes and bring yourself all the way back up. You can decide if you want to end the hypnosis here, or you can close/soften your eyes and send yourself back down into absorption again."

old: “If it is useful, attention may become more gathered. If it is not useful, I remain exactly as awake as I need to be.”
new: "When it's useful for me to deepen my absorption, I can. When it's not useful, I'm just as awake as I need to be."

old: Choose one simple scene: a room in the heart, a garden, a temple, a fire with the Protector nearby, a clear lake, or a chair where the adult waits. One scene is plenty.
new: Then you can do a room in your heart, or a garden, or a temple, or sitting next to a fire with your Protector nearby, or floating on a clear lake, or sitting in a chair, etc. Don't do more than one of these.

old: “Who or what needs to speak first?”
new: See who or what wants to talk to you first.

old: “As I wait, I give up the responsibility of making anything happen.
new: Give up all responsibility for making it happen.

old: If it is useful, the wise subconscious may let one finger twitch, pulse, lift, warm, tingle, or become subtly noticeable when the inner meeting space is ready.
new: "When my wise subconscious knows that I am at the meeting space inside myself that it wants to talk to me at, it can make one of my fingers twitch, or pulse, or lift up, or feel warm, or tingly, or somehow different, if it wants to."

old: I will not force it. I will not fake it. I will simply wait with love and notice.”
new: You're not going to make it happen or fake it. You're just going to wait with love for it to happen.

old: A finger may move, a hand may warm, the breath may change, or nothing may happen. None proves truth; at most, something may be listening.
new: It doesn't mean that anything will happen, but if something happens with one of your fingers, or you feel some other bodily change, it doesn't necessarily mean that it's real, but it does mean that something is listening to you.

old: Learn a useful induction and the full return below before developing a shortcut. My dad brought two fingers together in a mudra like the OK sign to help himself relax, including while driving. That’s his experience, not a recommendation to enter trance at the wheel. Keep alert calming and inward hypnosis on different cues.
new: Once you've learned some of the inductions on this website and also the bringing yourself all the way back down induction, you can make up your own shortcut for getting back under hypnosis. My dad used to do a mudra (hand sign) by bringing two fingers together in an "okay" sign, and it would help him relax. He even did it while driving, so don't use the same thing for calming yourself while driving as you do for going into inward hypnosis!

old: I’m speaking from experience in this appendix.

During self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, grief, prayer, plant-medicine-adjacent practice, or other altered states, people sometimes meet something that doesn’t feel like an ordinary emotion or younger part. It may appear as a demon, jinn, parasitic energy, dark intelligence, or terrifying archetype—a voice or image that feels intrusive, hateful, seductive, mocking, or simply alien.

I don’t need this guide to settle the metaphysics. Perhaps these are literal beings. Perhaps they are symbolic mind-forms, trauma in a frightening costume, dissociated energy, or ancestral and relational burdens. The practical question is:
“What response makes me safer, clearer, more loving, more grounded, and less hooked?”
new: I’m going to come from a bit more experience here.

Sometimes, during self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, extreme grief, prayer, or a variety of other altered states of consciousness, you may encounter something you perceive to be a demon, a jinn, a parasitic energy, some other kind of dark intelligence, or even a terrifying archetype. Sometimes it comes as a voice. Sometimes as an image. But it is not a simple emotion, and not merely a younger part.

First and foremost, it doesn’t matter for the purposes of this guide whether they are literally demons or not. All that matters is what the best way of dealing with them is, in terms of what leaves you feeling the safest, clearest, most loving, most grounded, etc.

old: When a demonic, jinn-like, hostile, or intrusive presence appears, don’t reward it with instant metaphysical certainty. Run the triage first: medical danger, environment, body, overload, and how open the mind has become. Open the eyes, feel the feet, name the room, lower stimulation, leave hostile company, and stop adding prompts. Don’t deepen, hunt for hidden truth, or debate ontology while destabilized.
“Only what can be integrated is welcome now. Anything too much can wait. The adult self remains present. The body may return to safety.”

Danger to self or others, psychosis-like fear, inability to sleep, extreme paranoia, chest pain, seizures, serious overheating, overdose concern, or loss of basic functioning means the self-hypnosis session is over. Get real-world help.
new: So what do you do when a demon, or jinn, or other bad or intrusive entity shows up? The same thing you do first for anything else— you check in with the room, your body, and safety in general.

“If there is anything that can be integrated right now, you may come forward. But know that you can wait, and that you will not be able to come forward until you are something that can be integrated. Know also that I will always be here as an adult, and that my body will bring you to a place of safety.”

If you feel like you’re in danger of hurting yourself or others, if you feel like you’re going psychotic and afraid, if you feel like you won’t be able to sleep afterwards, if you feel extremely paranoid, if you have chest pain, if you feel like you’re going to have a seizure, if you feel like you’re too hot in a serious way, if you feel like you’ve taken too much of something, or if you feel like you just can’t function in the world anymore, then the self-hypnosis session is over. Go get some real-world help.

old: Once you’re stable enough to stay present, notice what helps without turning the response into a metaphysical test. Put a hand on the heart if that feels welcome, take a comfortable breath, and keep the room available.
new: If not, then check in with yourself as to what will be the best response. Again, it doesn’t matter whether or not it’s literally a demon. Put your hand on your heart, if that feels

old: “I do not need to hate this. I do not need to merge with this. I do not need to obey this. I do not need to defeat this from fear. I return to loving awareness.”
new: SAY (aloud or internally): “I do not need to hate this. I do not need to merge with this. I do not need to obey this. I do not need to defeat this out of fear. I can come back into loving awareness.”

old: When the presence feels hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, or boundary-violating, don’t offer soft sentimental love as though inviting it in for tea. Use love with a boundary.

Sit upright. Press your feet into the floor. Let the spine rise. Gently draw the shoulder blades back so the chest is open but not exposed. Feel the skin boundary of the torso. Feel that this body has a perimeter.

“I recognize that suffering may be here, and I wish all suffering to return to the space where it belongs. But the boundary of this skin belongs to my adult life. You do not have permission to enter this house.”
“Compassion is present. The door is closed.”
new: IF YOU NEED A BODILY BOUNDARY WITH COMPASSION, CLOSE THE DOOR:
If the presence feels hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, violating, etc., you may not want to bring any kind of soft, sentimental love to this. You may want to bring a love that has a healthy boundary.
Sit up tall, press your feet into the floor, elongate your spine, pull your shoulder blades back gently. Feel your body’s skin-boundary – feel your torso’s boundary.
SAY (aloud or internally): “Even if there is suffering here, I wish for all suffering to go where it needs to go, but my skin-boundary is my adult body. You are not permitted in my house.”
Then say: “Even though I am feeling compassion, I am closing the door.”

old: A symbolic hostile-presence experience that settles with grounding and love is very different from a state that becomes persistent, paranoid, sleepless, dangerous, or impossible to reality-test.

If somebody believes they’re under attack for days, can’t sleep or function, hears commands, feels compelled to hurt themselves or anyone else, becomes manic, can’t communicate normally, or can’t distinguish symbolic experience from ordinary reality, stop treating the problem as hypnosis material. Get help.

If the practice makes you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, and functional, continue gently. If it makes you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated, frightened, or unreal, stop deepening and get support.
new: IF YOU THINK YOU ARE GOING PSYCHOTIC OR GETTING DE-STABILIZED:

There is a big difference between experiencing some symbolic “hostile presences” in yourself that settle with grounding and loving awareness, and going into a persistent state of paranoia, inability to sleep, danger to self or others, inability to communicate with others, inability to reality-test, mania, etc., etc.

If this work is making you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, functional, etc., then proceed. If it’s making you more paranoid, unable to sleep, grandiose, unable to communicate or function, afraid, unable to reality-test, etc., then don’t proceed and get help!

old: Hostile presences, shadow forces, grandiose parts, and altered-state imagery don’t always attack through fear. Sometimes they seduce through importance: a cosmic secret, a special mission, a vast download, a feeling of being uniquely chosen, or a revelation that makes washing dishes seem beneath your new rank.

“Thank you for the imagery. I do not require a grand performance. If this information cannot become a simple, honest act of care tomorrow morning — washing the dishes, cleaning my room, keeping a promise, apologizing, resting, eating, or helping someone I love — it is not useful to my path.”
new: THE “WASHING THE DISHES” TRICK FOR HALLOWED/COSMIC DOWNLOADS:
Sometimes these presences/shadows/parts try to convince you of their importance in other ways, such as by pretending to give you some “cosmic download.” To these, say:
“Unless the information you are giving me helps me to wash the dishes or clean my room or do something simple and loving for somebody, it’s not going to help me on my path.”

old: For sleep hypnosis, use Nimja’s sleep playlist.
new: If you’re using this for help getting to sleep, try it with one of Nimja’s sleep playlists.

old: Preview the sequence, choose one purpose, and decide whether you want to begin. Each family can be light, eyes-open, or replaced by no-trance contact. Notice the actual response—including no change—and let it determine the next move. Move, imagine, change the sensory channel, remain still, or stop. Use the complete waking return after every induction.
new: What are you going to do next in the sequence? Do you want to do it at all? If you’re using a family of inductions, have you tried the lighter ones, or doing it with your eyes open, or even just doing no-trance contact in place of the trance induction? What happened when you tried to do it (even if it seemed that nothing happened)? What’s the next thing to try – something new, moving your body, using imagery, using a different sensory channel, just sitting still for a while, giving up on it…? Do you need to bring yourself fully awake out of the induction?

old: If vivid images don’t come, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial sense, touch, movement, or simple knowing. The mind doesn’t owe anybody a movie.
new: NOTE: If you’re not able to generate imagery with any vividness, you can translate the metaphors into words, rhythms, spatial, touch, movement, or even just knowing concepts.

old: Hear the actual room and feel the body before imagining a step toward a chosen destination. Use footsteps, textures, or landmarks to gather attention. Change scenery or skip directly to dialogue when useful. Notice a detail without assigning hidden meaning; the mystery is how the scene develops, not what will be done to you. Who or what needs to speak? Return by the same route and close the imagined space.
new: Listen to the sounds of the room you are currently in and feel your body. Now imagine yourself walking somewhere, where do you want to go? As you walk, listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings. What texture are the objects you pass? What landmarks do you see? Now that you've collected enough attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where you can directly speak to whoever/whatever it is you want to speak to. Or you can just cut straight to the chase if you want. Observe what you want to observe, just don't make it into a "what are they going to do to you?" kind of thing. When you're ready to finish, imagine walking back the way you came and close the space.

old: Ask how the experience is represented. What changes when the image moves two feet back, the voice gets quieter, or the edge becomes less sharp?
new: Things to ask yourself when representing something. What would happen if you did something else.

old: “I am not deleting the signal. I am adjusting the volume so I can listen without being overwhelmed.”
new: "I am not deleting it just adjusting the volume."

old: Before moving one imaginary pixel, ask the guard whether that change is acceptable.
new: Before you do anything imagine moving a pixel and ask your guard if it is ok to do this.

old: “Would it be okay if we moved this image back just a little, or lowered the volume slightly, purely so my adult self can stay present enough to hear what you need to tell me?”
new: "Is it ok that I move the image back two feet, quiet the voice down, make the edges less sharp so that I can do this, the adult me, to hear what you have got to say?"

old: An anchor is a cue connected to a state: a hand on the heart, two fingers touching, a breath, a word, a posture, scent, or song. Find a real state you want easier access to, feel it, and pair the cue while it is clearly present with the phrase, “This is available.” For hypnotic re-entry, choose a usable receptive state rather than peak emotional intensity; follow “A shortcut back into hypnosis” in the main induction section. Keep alert calming and the synchronicity wake-up cue separate.
new: There are lots of ways to anchor something. Put your hand on your heart, touch two fingers together, use a breath, a word, body posture, smell, song, anything. Feel something that you have got to in reality that you want to get back to easily. As you feel it do the anchor thing and say to yourself that this is what you are anchoring and it is available to you. Make sure you do it when you have clearly got it. To get back into a hypnotic state easily don't go for a peak emotional state but find a good receptive state that you can use. See the main induction section on a shortcut back into hypnosis. Make sure that this is separate from the alert, calming, synchronicity wake up thing.

old: Don’t end with “I understand.” Ask where life will test the understanding, picture the actual cue, and rehearse the smallest better response.
“If [cue], then I [small action].”
new: 1. Do some future pacing (check out this video ) to make sure that the new insight holds, by imagining some future situations where the old behavior would have triggered.
If they appear, practice a new small behavior by setting up an implementation intention ("If...then..."):

old: Classic NLP uses the Swish to replace an old self-image with a new one. Done mechanically, it can feel like an inner eviction. Here, the old pattern stays visible, the new possibility stands beside it, and I notice the body’s response while comparing what each future would actually require.
new: 2. Use a variation of the Swish Pattern from NLP, where instead of pushing out the old pattern, allowing it to stay there, just make sure that the old and the new pattern are both visible, feel the bodily sensations that arise, and see if there is anything the new pattern requires from in the future, that the old one didn't.

old: Open your eyes. Move. Touch something textured. Name five objects. End the deeper practice for the day.
new: Open your eyes, move your body, feel something textured, and name five objects out loud. Then finish up for the day.

old: Return to food, sleep, chores, humility, and somebody who will disagree with you.
“If this insight is real, it will survive sleep, food, time, humility, and feedback.”
new: Go eat some food, go to sleep, do chores, accept some humility, get some feedback.
Silently say, “I need to know that these insights can survive sleep, food, time, humility, and feedback.”

old: When the practice turns into a technical performance, stop improving it. Put one hand on the heart and one on the solar plexus.
“I am not here to do this perfectly. I am here to be in relationship with what is deeper than my surface mind.”
“What would make this feel more like communion and less like performance?”
Silence may be the answer. Rest may be the answer. One honest action may be the answer. Take the answer that actually arrived.
new: Stop trying to do the practice better. Put one hand on your heart and one on your solar plexis and say,
“I’m not supposed to be doing this well. I’m supposed to be entering into relationship with what’s deeper than my surface mind.
“What would help me turn this into a communion rather than a performance?”
Sometimes the answer is to be silent, to rest, to do something. Do the thing that comes to you.

old: Ask the bliss to become specific.
“What task, boundary, meal, rest, repair, or conversation does love require next?”
new: Bring it down to a specific level.
“What would love do right now?”

old: Don’t pry.
“Show me the capacity before the content.”
new: Refrain. Say, “First show me the capacity, and you can show me the content later.”

old: Sit up and open your eyes.
“What real action is this fantasy replacing?”
new: Sit up and open your eyes. Then ask, “What real action am I avoiding with this fantasy?”

old: “Where has divine love not yet descended into the wound?”

A genuine opening can show you a depth of love or freedom you hadn’t known was possible. Let that matter without demanding the child receive it on command. Prayer can also evoke abandonment or condemnation, or a teacher’s betrayal can damage something sacred. Ask what was lost and what needs questioning; more of the same practice isn’t automatically the answer.

Sometimes practical care helps while the available horizon of life still feels too small. Curiosity about deeper happiness is worth following without pretending to believe an explanation. Other people already have enough love and meaning for the life they want. Spirituality doesn’t need to become another assignment.
new: Ask, “Where is divine love not yet descending to meet my pain?”

You may have had a genuinely profound opening that revealed to you how much more love and freedom are possible. It’s also possible that, as a child, you prayed and then felt abandoned or condemned; that you went to a teacher and were betrayed. It’s worth asking some questions about what happened. But doing more of the same may not be the answer.

Sometimes the best thing is to do something practical in your life, while pretending that there isn’t a larger horizon, but pretending that you’re curious about what it would be like to step into it. Other people seem to have enough love and meaning. You don’t have to do anything about it. Spirituality doesn’t have to be another thing you’re supposed to do.

old: A real wound and a checking loop can coexist. Ask whether this round helps you feel, understand, decide, or respond differently—or whether you’re checking the same question for reassurance. Grief and practice can revisit familiar ground; novelty isn’t required every time.

When it is a checking loop, let the thought remain without arguing with it or chasing it away, and return to a chosen activity or relationship. You don’t have to hold an inner meeting every time a thought appears or complete a ritual before you’re allowed to live.
“What direction would the Leader choose now?”
new: You may have a real wound to deal with, but you may also have a checking loop. Ask yourself, “Am I looking for something new here, or am I checking again to see if it’s gone yet?” Sometimes, both in grieving and in practice, you’re supposed to cover the same ground over and over again.

If you discover that you are in a checking loop, then let the thought be there but don’t argue with it. Return to some chosen activity or relationship. You don’t have to hold a meeting with every thought that arises. You don’t have to do some magical thing before you can start your life.
Ask yourself, “What would the Leader do?”

old: “What would prove to the inner child that the adult is real?”
Then do the thing.
new: Ask, “What would show my child that I’m for real?”
Then do it.
